notes.title: A Message from the Developer [Release Time, Presskit]
notes.content:
Orrstead officially releases [b]March 7 at 12am EST[/b]!

[u][b]Message to the Community[/b][/u]
I've been working on this game for the past 4 years, and am very excited for people to check out my first major release. Orrstead has evolved dramatically over the years, and I'm proud of what it has become.

Thank you to community members who have supported the game and volunteered their time to test the game and provide feedback.

[b][u]Launch Day[/u][/b]
While I've been testing the game to ensure a smooth launch, this is the first time a (much larger) player base will be experiencing the game, so I expect there will be some unanticipated bugs. If you experience any, report them in the [url=https://discord.gg/eEY75Nqk3C]Discord[/url] and I'll work to fix them ASAP.

Aside from that, I'm very excited to see your gameplay, reviews, and what you think of the game!

[u][b]Presskit[/b][/u]
If you are a reviewer / content creator, you can find the presskit here: [url=https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1vG5GuQYUav8GzsR-Jz4BVQgvalsjLoAN?usp=sharing]drive[/url]


IndividualKex

p.s. don't forget to build tax collectors

notes.title: Alpha 0.10 - Road to Release
notes.content:
[b]Mechanics Overhaul[/b]
This update features an overhaul to resource management, adding much more depth to the resource management.

[b]Core Features[/b]
In conjunction with the resource management improvements, railroads have been added to the game. These are experimental, with the first rendition available on the demo.

[b]Release Date[/b]
With the core mechanics and systems stable, further development will focus on adding content. The release date will be...

[b]March 7, 2024[/b]

notes.title: Alpha 0.8 - Pillars of Prosperity
notes.content:
This update focuses on the introduction of several [b]Unique Buildings[/b]. Each of these buildings double the wisdom gained from the respective resource, as well as other provide other unique bonuses.

Bread (2x wisdom from each)
[list]
[*] [b]Grand Bakery[/b]: Upgrades nearby Village Houses to [b]Baker's Residences[/b], which have higher happiness and produce a bit of wheat.
[*] [b]Grand Oven[/b]: Must be built near Grand Bakery.
[*] [b]Grain Mill[/b]: +50% efficiency to nearby Farms.
[*] [b]Grain Silo[/b]: Must be built near Grain Mill. Stores 250 Wheat.
[*] [b]Baker's Guild[/b]: Must be built near Grand Bakery. Increases happiness of nearby households.
[/list]

Fish (2x wisdom from each)
[list]
[*] [b]Fisherman's Wharf[/b]: Supplies boats to nearby Docks, doubling their efficiency.
[*] [b]Harbormaster[/b]: Must be built near Fisherman's Wharf. Increases happiness of nearby households.
[*] [b]Lighthouse[/b]: Must be built on a peninsula. Provides +1 global happiness.
[/list]

These new builds are accompanied with sweeping balance changes, as well as minor UI tweaks and bugfixes.

notes.title: Alpha 0.25 Patch Notes
notes.content:
This update, unlike prefix minor updates, introduces minor gameplay tweaks.

I felt that lumberjack houses were a bit confusing and not very interesting, while farm houses were pretty fun and intuitive. So, I've changed lumberjack houses from wood-to-wisdom converts to something that upgrades nearby lumberjacks, similar to the farm house.

I also think that it feels better to get wisdom constantly from more sources, so I've made both farms and lumberjacks provide wisdom, and increased the wisdom-per-level a bit to balance it out. It's kind of fun now to watch wisdom fly in from all over the place.

I also tested a Workshop building that converts wood to fine wood, and made fine wood a requirement for some buildings such as the tavern. However, in testing, it just felt like an added step that wasn't very fun, so I reverted it.

[list]
[*] Reworked building: [b]Lumberjack House[/b] now upgrades nearby lumberjacks, but no longer converts wood to wisdom
[*] Reworked building: [b]Lumberjack[/b] now has reduced radius and requirements, requires a worker, and provides wisdom

notes.title: Alpha 0.2 Released
notes.content:
[b]Orrstead 0.2 is now available [url=https://individualkex.itch.io/orrstead]on itch.io[/url], rebuilt from the ground up![/b]

This is a major update, laying the foundation for the future of Orrstead. The benefits of this rebuilt codebase are:
[list]
[*] Improved performance
[*] Mod support
[*] Custom asset support
[*] Localization (currently English/Swedish)
[*] Faster iteration on future updates
[/list]
In addition, there have been major changes to the core mechanics of the game:
[list]
[*] Global [b]wisdom[/b] resource, similar to experience, streamlining progression and unlocking of new buildings
[*] Removed the phase system
[*] Introduced [b]adjacency rules[/b] and [b]bonuses[/b], such as the lumberjack requiring nearby trees, or the tavern upgrading nearby houses
[*] Buildings now follow automatic upgrade paths, such as a farm upgrading to an efficient farm when near a farm house, producing wheat faster
[*] Updated visuals/tuning for all buildings
[*] Reworked UI, focusing on minimalism and extendibility (may be reworked again for better visuals later in development)
[/list]
In the coming months, I'm looking to increase transparency and community involvement on mid-and-late-game iteration. If you are interested, [url=https://discord.gg/eEY75Nqk3C]join the discord[/url].

notes.title: Orrstead 0.2 Overhaul Underway
notes.content:
​Hi everyone, writing a formal update here on what I've been doing!

[b]​tl;dr: Rebuilding the foundations of Orrstead to be faster and moddable.[/b]

​The past few months, I have been experimenting with different gameplay features for Phase 2 of the game. It takes quite a while to iterate systems, and I've been dissatisfied with a lot of the ones I've tried. I think that in the long-term, it's best that I shift my approach.

As a solution, I've decided to rebuild the foundations of the game to be much easier to extend, both for me and modders, making it much easier to test features. I've learned a lot since I started Orrstead, and have an idea of how the core systems can be much more efficient. So, I'm doing that!

I'm mostly happy with the gameplay of Phase 1, so the gameplay won't change drastically. I'll be focusing mostly on finishing up the core systems rebuild. I'll try to get this out sooner rather than later, so I can get the community more involved in the development.

If you'd like to participate, come join the discord! A community focused around game dev, with channels for Orrstead feedback/discussion: https://discord.gg/eEY75Nqk3C

notes.title: Alpha Update 0.11
notes.content:
Alpha 0.11 Patch Notes! 
This alpha build is currently available for playtesting, free [url=https://individualkex.itch.io/orrstead]on itch.io[/url].

[u][b]Major Gameplay Changes[/b][/u]
To prepare for Phase 2, the way happiness works has been revamped. 

Happiness will now decrease linearly as population increases. Happiness bonuses (previously just the tavern) are no longer based on average household happiness. This made it feel like a penalty to build new houses (that don't have a tavern), instead of being an interesting choice. So now, happiness will increase for every tavern built, but with diminishing returns (logarithmically).

The idea is that because the population penalty is linear and bonuses are logarithmic, you will need to keep finding new ways to increase happiness, rather than by just spamming taverns. In Phase 2, I want these systems to be complex enough to allow interesting decisions, and make room for creativity. For now in Phase 1, I've added a new system that will move things in this direction: housing upgrades.

[u][b]Housing Upgrades[/b][/u]
Housing now starts off at Tier 1, and every house has an Appeal, based on factors like having neighbors, a path, water, and a tavern. When appeal reaches a threshold, the house can be upgraded to Tier 2 for a wood cost. Each Tier 2 house will boost happiness (with diminishing returns).

I'm still experimenting with these changes, but this mechanic is intended to be integral to future (phase 2 onward) mechanics. I'm still not certain if I want to move forward with this system, I could see it being tedious to keep upgrading housing, or it might be fun. Let me know what you think, and if you have any suggestions!

[u][b]Minor Changes[/b][/u]
[list]
[*] Citizens will now construct buildings in the order they're placed.
[*] Citizens will change jobs immediately when priority is changed.
[*] UI for selected buildings redesigned, allowing space for more UI elements in the future.
[*] Level of detail added for several models.
[*] Audio settings added.
[*] Graphics preset added (currently just quality and performance presets, more graphics options will be added later).
[*] UI X button is now easier to click.
[*] Minor save/load menu changes.
[*] Citizens will now look for a home immediately, instead of a few minutes after arriving.
[*] Minor graphics optimizations for lower-end machines.
[*] Lots of other small changes I forgot.
[/list]

notes.title: The First Alpha
notes.content:
[b][u]Announcement[/u][/b]
Hello all! I've been working on this strategy game solo for a couple years now, and am excited to be releasing the first public-facing build [url=https://individualkex.itch.io/orrstead]here on itch.io[/url].

[u][b]Development Status[/b][/u]
This is an alpha build - Alpha 0.1? Alpha 0.1. This contains only the first phase of the game, and is intended for playtesting and feedback on the core mechanics. Your feedback and bug reports are highly appreciated.

[u][b]Future Plans[/b][/u]
The game will have three gameplay phases, with each phase introducing more technology, resources, and mechanics. Only the first phase has been developed, and I really want to solidify the foundation of the game before expanding into future phases. Immediate development plans are:
[olist]
[*] Based on feedback, make adjustments to the current Phase 1 gameplay loop.
[*] Implement various planned improvements to Phase 1, including visuals, audio, UI, etc.
[*] Lay out roadmap for Phase 2.
[/olist]
[u][b]Release Date[/b][/u]
When it's ready, which won't be this year. After a couple years of experimental development and trying different gameplay mechanics, the game has settled into a scope and core gameplay loop that I believe is fun, and that I'm confident in being able to finish as a solo developer. However, the game is still early in development, and I can't confidently give a release date yet.
